summary.title: Learn Vimscript the Hard Way
summary.one_liner: You learn how to customize Vim with a vimrc and then write Vimscript programs, from mappings and options up to building and distributing a full plugin.
keywords: how to write a vim plugin
takeaways: Customize Vim quickly using settings, mappings, abbreviations and autocommands in your ~/.vimrc
Understand Vimscript as a programming language: variables, scoping, conditionals, functions, lists, dictionaries and loops
Learn how to structure and document a plugin, including filetype detection, syntax highlighting, folding, autoloading and distribution
Prerequisite: you should already be comfortable editing text in Vim and know terms like buffer, window and insert mode
summary.summary: This free online book by Steve Losh (copyright 2013) teaches Vim users how to customize Vim with Vimscript. It is split into three parts: basic vimrc customization, Vimscript as a programming language, and a worked example of creating a plugin for distribution. It is explicitly not a guide to using Vim, so readers are expected to already be comfortable editing text. The page lists the chapter outline and notes that the HTML version is free to read, with paid ebook and print editions available.
